subject.title: fix(cron): default deleteAfterRun for isolated cron jobs

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs default to cleanup/deleteAfterRun across fresh and existing persisted jobs, or should recurring deleteAfterRun remain a one-shot-only invalid contract?
rationale: This PR and the open strict-validation PR encode opposite cron lifecycle contracts, and automation cannot safely choose the product/API direction for existing user jobs.

options.title: Complete recurring cleanup contract
options.body: Keep this PR's direction, but require persisted omitted-job handling and tests before merge.

options.title: Choose one-shot-only validation
options.body: Pause or close this PR and continue through the strict-validation path after caller and upgrade recovery are complete.

options.title: Accept fresh-create-only behavior
options.body: Allow the default only for newly normalized jobs and explicitly document or track the existing-job gap.

recommendation.title: Complete recurring cleanup contract
recommendation.body: Keep this PR's direction, but require persisted omitted-job handling and tests before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent history across cron normalization, store conversion, and repository policy for compatibility-sensitive defaults.
